1.2.3.6-r1.burton_quote: that subjects himself to fear, desire, grief, ambition, shame, is not happy, but altogether miserable, tortured with continual labour, care, and misery

1.2.3.6-r2.burton_quote: Many men neglect the tumults of the world, and care not for glory, and yet they are afraid of infamy, repulse, disgrace (Tul. offic. lib. 1), they can severely contemn pleasure, bear grief indifferently, but they are quite battered and broken with reproach and obloquy

1.2.3.6-r3.burton_quote: because he could not unfold the fisherman’s riddle

1.2.3.6-r4.burton_quote: Sophocles killed himself, for that a Tragedy of his, was hissed off the stage

1.2.3.6-r5.burton_quote: after he was overcome of his enemy, for three days space sat solitary in the fore-part of the Ship, abstaining from all company, even of Cleopatra herself, and afterwards for very shame, butchered himself

1.2.3.6-r6.burton_quote: wilfully banished himself, forsaking his country, and all his dear friends, because he was out in reciting his Poems
1.2.3.6-r6.translation: The poem he recited badly was his Argonautica, and he went into exile for shame.

1.2.3.6-r7.burton_quote: Hostratus the Friar took that book which Reuchlin had writ against him, under the name of Epist. obscurorum virorum, so to heart, that for shame and grief he made away himself
